data.title: DEVELOPMENT OF A METHOD FOR CLASSIFYING POWER TRANSFORMER DEFECTS BASED ON DISSOLVED GAS ANALYSIS

data.abstract:
Relevance
The article considers the problem of automated identification of power
transformer defects based on dissolved gas analysis of transformer oil. As a
solution, a method based on processing the composition of dissolved gases is
proposed. The method includes input data control, bringing analysis results
to a unified form, calculating diagnostic indicators, forming a feature set and
calibrating probabilistic estimates of the power transformer defect
classification result. The software implementation of the method is based on
a gradient boosting model over decision trees and an extended set of
diagnostic features, including gas concentrations, gas ratios, normalized
shares and aggregated gas composition indicators.
The quality of the method was assessed using stratified k-fold crossvalidation.
The obtained metric values confirm the applicability of the
implemented method as part of a decision support system for diagnosing the
technical condition of power transformers.
Aim of research
The aim of the research is to develop a method for identifying power
transformer defects based on dissolved gas analysis, providing formalized
processing of gas composition, formation of a diagnostically significant
feature set and calibration of probabilistic estimates of the result for further
use in a decision support system.
Research methods
The following analytical techniques were applied in this work:
chromatographic analysis of gases dissolved in transformer oil; processing
and normalization of diagnostic data; calculation of gas ratios; and
computation of aggregated gas composition indicators. Defect classification
was performed using gradient boosting based on decision trees (LightGBM
library), followed by sigmoid calibration of the probabilistic outputs. Model
performance was assessed using the macro-averaged F1-score, balanced
accuracy, Matthew’s correlation coefficient, and LogLoss, with stratified
k-fold cross-validation (k = 5) employed to preserve the original defect type
distribution across the training and validation subsets.
Results
A methodology for classifying power transformer defects based on the
results of chromatographic analysis of gases dissolved in transformer oil is
proposed, together with a corresponding software implementation. The
diagnostic output includes the defect type and its associated probabilistic
estimates according to the adopted classification framework. The calibration
of probability estimates enables the determination of the confidence level in
the diagnostic result and facilitates the ranking of alternative defect types by
their likelihood. The developed methodology and software can be integrated
into a decision support system and utilized for expert assessment of the
technical condition of power transformers.

data.title: The State of the Art in transformer fault diagnosis with artificial intelligence and Dissolved Gas Analysis: A Review of the Literature

openAccessPdf.disclaimer: Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.11880, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use.

data.abstract: Transformer fault diagnosis (TFD) is a critical aspect of power system maintenance and management. This review paper provides a comprehensive overview of the current state of the art in TFD using artificial intelligence (AI) and dissolved gas analysis (DGA). The paper presents an analysis of recent advancements in this field, including the use of deep learning algorithms and advanced data analytics techniques, and their potential impact on TFD and the power industry as a whole. The review also highlights the benefits and limitations of different approaches to transformer fault diagnosis, including rule-based systems, expert systems, neural networks, and machine learning algorithms. Overall, this review aims to provide valuable insights into the importance of TFD and the role of AI in ensuring the reliable operation of power systems.

data.title: An Anomaly Diagnosis and Prediction Method for Dissolved Gases in Transformer Oil Based on Multi-Expert Learning

Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use.

data.abstract: As a core component of power grids, the operational status of oil-immersed transformers is directly linked to the safety and stability of the entire power system. Dissolved Gas Analysis (DGA) has been widely used to assess internal faults in transformers. However, existing methods often rely on single-model learning, which struggles to capture the complex couplings and nonlinear dynamics among multiple gas components, leading to limited prediction accuracy and anomaly detection capability. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel anomaly diagnosis and concentration prediction method for dissolved gases in transformer oil based on a multi-expert learning mechanism. The proposed system integrates three complementary expert models: the anomaly-aware expert identifies and repairs abnormal points in historical gas concentration sequences; the temporal modeling expert captures the dynamic evolution of gas concentrations over time; and the context-aware expert models the latent interactions among different gas components. A gated fusion mechanism is designed to adaptively assign weights to each expert according to the input context, enabling robust multi-dimensional feature integration and reliable prediction. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms traditional single-model approaches under various transformer operating conditions, offering strong support for equipment condition monitoring and intelligent maintenance.

data.title: Transformer Fault Diagnosis via Fourier Neural Operator and Graph Neural Network Fusion

openAccessPdf.disclaimer: Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://api.unpaywall.org/v2/10.1109/NPSIF68783.2025.11386309?email=<INSERT_YOUR_EMAIL> or https://doi.org/10.1109/NPSIF68783.2025.11386309, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. data.abstract: Accurate diagnosis of transformer faults is essential for ensuring the secure and stable operation of power systems. Conventional approaches based on dissolved gas analysis (DGA) typically rely on expert knowledge and often fail to capture complex nonlinear relationships. To address these limitations, this work introduces a dual-channel deep learning fusion framework for intelligent fault-type identification in transformers. The proposed architecture processes both temporal and structural aspects of gas data in parallel: one channel employs a Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) to model the temporal evolution of key gas concentrations, thereby capturing long-term dynamic patterns, while the other channel leverages a Graph Neural Network (GNN) to represent the relational structure among gas species, extracting their inherent coupling characteristics. A fusion layer subsequently integrates the temporal representation from the FNO channel with the structural representation from the GNN channel to produce final diagnostic outcomes. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that the proposed fusion model achieves superior diagnostic accuracy compared with conventional single-model methods.
